newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland mayor announces support for school levy.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland mayor announces support for school levy.

text.p: Cleveland Mayor Michael White announced Wednesday that he will support a 13.5 mill property tax levy on the Nov. 5 ballot for the city's public schools.
White's endorsement followed that of Ohio Gov. George Voinovich on Tuesday.

White said he had received assurances from school officials that the money raised by the levy hike would be "well spent and well managed and that measures would be taken to hold the district publicly accountable for the use of levy dollars."
In August, a U.S. District Court judge in Cleveland ordered the proposed operating levy hike to be placed on the ballot after the Cleveland school board rejected a referendum to increase the levy.
The levy proposal was supported by the Ohio Department of Education, which took control of the schools in March 1995.
State officials have said the levy was needed to improve services and to start paying off about $87 million of the school system's operating debt.
The 13.5 mill hike in the property tax levy would raise about $67.5 million a year. Cleveland voters last passed an operating levy for the schools in November 1983.
